source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Diagnose acute coronary syndrome from the telephone history and provide a definitive diagnosis to the caller.","B":"Perform a focused assessment, recognize a possible emergency, and direct urgent evaluation according to protocol and scope.","C":"Complete a detailed lifetime history before deciding whether emergency evaluation is needed.","D":"Recommend a prescription drug for chest pain without an authorized order, protocol, or prescriber involvement."}}
source_row.rationale: Telephone triage requires nursing assessment and clinical judgment within scope, not remote definitive diagnosis or unauthorized prescribing. New chest pressure with dyspnea can represent an emergency, so Option B appropriately prioritizes urgent evaluation. A exceeds the information available, C delays care, and D exceeds scope absent an authorized mechanism.
source_row.source_detail: Management of Care activity statements: establish priorities for care, facilitate referrals and follow-up, collaborate with the interprofessional team, use resources, and provide care within legal scope; clinical judgment is integrated throughout the plan. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.stem: A telephone-triage nurse receives a caller reporting new chest pressure and shortness of breath. Which action best reflects the RN's role?
